The largest financings went to Tenstorrent, a developer of AI processors and systems, and AI lab Flapping Airplanes. The quirkiest round, meanwhile, was undoubtedly a $200 million financing for Warhound, which wants to breed elite military dogs. A number of big rounds in areas including biotech, space tech and physical AI rounded out the list.

articles.title: Senators say targeted ads are a security risk. Ad groups say the critics are off base.
articles.description: Citizen Lab’s AdFection findings have senators pushing for industry improvements, while IAB Europe and Google defend their vetting practices. The post Senators say targeted ads are a security risk. Ad groups say the critics are off base. appeared first on CyberScoop .

articles.title: Protecting Trade Secrets In The Age Of AI
articles.description: AI agents create new trade secret risks by allowing employees to access expertise or inadvertently expose proprietary information through personal devices. In this guest commentary, Seth Kugler, a partner at Grellas Shah LLP, warns companies that they should adopt strict AI policies, restrict data access on unmanaged devices, update confidentiality agreements, and act immediately when misuse is suspected.

articles.title: 5 Interesting Startup Deals You May Have Missed: Robot Training, Space Lasers And Greener Cement
articles.description: From teaching robots to do everyday household chores to using lasers to track satellites in space, this month's crop of interesting startup deals spans some decidedly different corners of tech.

articles.title: The AI IPO Wave Is The Dot-Com Bubble’s Evil Twin. Anthropic’s Delay Just Proved It.
articles.description: In this guest article from Airrived co-founder and CEO Anurag Gurtu, he contends that Anthropic’s rapid revenue growth does not justify its proposed $2 trillion IPO valuation, given enormous infrastructure commitments, safety concerns, customer concentration and competition from cheaper open-weight models, saying instead that lasting enterprise AI value will come from proprietary data, reliable deployment and measurable customer outcomes rather than expensive models alone.

articles.title: Acquirers Are Snapping Up Boom-Era Startups That Haven’t Raised Funding In Years
articles.description: A number of companies whose names might feature on a playlist of 2021 boom-era unicorns have sold to acquirers in recent months, including one-time highfliers like Airtable, Headspace and Miro. In many cases, companies are selling at valuations which, while not puny, are still far below their former peaks.

articles.title: Your Next Customer Might Be An Agent. Here’s How To Build Your Brand For Both Humans And AI.
articles.description: As AI agents increasingly recommend and purchase products, brands must appeal to both machines and humans by documenting their voice, creating clear product descriptions and checking how AI summarizes their messaging. Guest author Toby Coulthard suggests that startups should build these practices in from the outset, preserving human appeal while measuring success through conversions and revenue rather than content volume.

articles.title: When A Startup Sells, Its Employees’ Equity Plans Can Change Overnight
articles.description: Startup acquisitions can reshape employees’ finances and careers, with individual outcomes depending on a variety of conditions. Guest author Ron Honig, co-CEO and managing partner of From-Honig Family Office, suggests that before making major life changes, employees should clarify their award rights, when proceeds will become available, and what their after-tax payout can realistically support.

We also discussed how ownership stakes and secondary transactions have shaped the firm’s approach to returning capital.
